reference_answer: 20 days per year under the current policy effective January 2026, which supersedes the older 15-day policy.

question: I have a business meal receipt from 45 days ago that I haven't submitted yet. Can I still get reimbursed?
reference_answer: Expenses submitted 31-90 days after incurrence may be reimbursed at your manager's discretion but are not guaranteed. You should submit it as soon as possible and your manager will review whether to approve it, though there is no guarantee of reimbursement at this point.

question: I'm in the Data & Analytics department and want to work from home most of the time. What do I need to do to get approval for a fully remote arrangement?
reference_answer: Data & Analytics roles are flexible with typically 1-2 days on-site, and full remote work is available for Data & Analytics positions with VP-level approval and a 6-month probationary period. You should discuss the arrangement with your direct manager, complete the Remote Work Agreement form from the Confluence template, and submit it to HR via Workday by the 15th of the prior month for approval within 5 business days.

question: Can I share patient health information on our internal Slack channel if it's just with my team?
reference_answer: No, patient health information (PHI) must never be shared outside authorized channels. All ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, and PulseBoard data must remain confidential, and violations may result in termination and legal action.

question: What laptop options will I receive as a new hire, and when will it be ready for my first day?
reference_answer: You will receive either a MacBook Pro (M2, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) or a Dell XPS 15 (Intel i7, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) based on your role and team preference. Your laptop will be imaged and ready before your first day of employment, as equipment is provisioned by Day 1.

question: Can I use my personal laptop to access ClaimsFlow from home?
reference_answer: No, you must use a company laptop only. Personal devices cannot access ClaimsFlow or CareBridge. Additionally, you should use the company VPN when working from home, with setup instructions available in Confluence under IT-SETUP.

question: When can I enroll in benefits after I'm hired, and when will my coverage start?
reference_answer: New hires have a separate 30-day enrollment window beginning on their first day of employment. Your benefits coverage will become effective on the first of the month following 30 days of employment, assuming you're a full-time employee working 30+ hours weekly.

question: How long does it typically take for a provider to receive payment after a claim is approved?
reference_answer: Approved claims move to Payment Batch status and are processed nightly at 11 PM ET. Payments typically reach provider bank accounts within 2-3 business days, and you can verify payment confirmation by checking TimeTrax under Reports > Payment History.

question: Who should I contact if a claim keeps getting rejected with the same denial code?
reference_answer: You should escalate to the Claims Ops manager, Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@meridian.local), if the same claim is rejected twice. Additionally, if you're unsure about the rejection code or the payer hasn't responded after 10 days, Sarah Chen should also be contacted for guidance.

question: How often should I set my report to refresh, and what's the recommended time?
reference_answer: You can set your report refresh frequency to Hourly, Daily, or Weekly. The document recommends setting Daily refreshes for 2 AM, and you can also configure email notifications to stakeholders when the report updates.

question: What should I do if I left work early one day and need to submit different hours than what was scheduled?
reference_answer: You should enter your actual hours worked in the 'Hours Worked' column, which may differ from scheduled hours if you left early, came in late, or worked overtime. For example, if you were scheduled 8 hours but left 30 minutes early for a medical appointment, you would enter 7.5 hours. It's also recommended to use the 'Notes' field to explain the reason for the deviation.

question: Who should I contact if I need help accessing the Snowflake database, and what will they do?
reference_answer: You should contact DBA Priya Mehta, who will schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the Snowflake instance for you. The connection string you'll need is analytics-prod.snowflakecomputing.com.

question: How long will it take to get my dataset after I submit a request?
reference_answer: The timeline depends on the priority level you select: Routine requests take 5-7 business days, Urgent requests take 2-3 business days, and Blocking requests are completed by the next business day. Data & Analytics reviews new requests every Monday and Thursday, and they typically respond with questions or assignment within 1 business day.

question: What time should I schedule a ClaimsFlow deployment and how much downtime should I tell the Claims Ops team to expect?
reference_answer: Deployments typically occur on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 2-4 PM ET to minimize impact on Claims Ops. You should notify the team that the expected downtime is 15 minutes.

question: How many claims does ClaimsFlow process each month, and which major payers does it integrate with?
reference_answer: ClaimsFlow processes approximately 12,000–15,000 claims monthly across Meridian Health Partners' managed care and administrative services contracts. The system integrates with major payers including Aetna, Cigna, and UnitedHealth.

question: How long does it typically take for a claim to be processed from submission to payment?
reference_answer: A typical claim takes 8-12 business days from submission to either approval or denial. Approved claims are then batched and paid via ACH transfer with a 2-3 day settlement time, meaning the full cycle from submission to payment is generally 10-15 business days.

question: What time does CareBridge send its daily batch files to ClaimsFlow, and what format are they in?
reference_answer: CareBridge sends daily batch files to ClaimsFlow at 2:00 AM EST via SFTP in CSV format. The files include patient ID, service date, service code, provider NPI, units of service, and authorization reference, and follow the naming convention carebridge_claims_YYYYMMDD.csv.

question: How often do the reports on PulseBoard get updated, and are there any exceptions?
reference_answer: Most PulseBoard reports refresh daily at 2 AM EST. However, there are exceptions: the Patient Engagement Metrics report refreshes weekly on Mondays due to data processing delays in CareBridge, and some reports may have stale data if their owners are unavailable (for example, the Denial Analysis Dashboard has not been updated since January 2024).

question: What's the deadline for submitting my timesheet each week, and what happens if I miss it?
reference_answer: Timesheets must be submitted by 5 PM Friday each week. If you submit after this deadline, your timesheet will be flagged as late and may delay payroll processing by one cycle.

question: Who should I reach out to if I'm joining the team that manages our claims processing system?
reference_answer: Marcus Chen leads the ClaimsFlow Team, which owns the end-to-end claims processing system including the API layer, database schema, and batch processing jobs. The team consists of 12 engineers and uses Node.js and PostgreSQL with deployments to AWS via GitHub Actions.

question: I just finished coding a feature and need to move my ticket forward. What status should I put it in before marking it as Done?
reference_answer: Move your ticket to 'In Review' status, where code review happens. Do not skip this step—tickets stuck in In Review for 3+ days get flagged in standup, so make sure to get your code reviewed before moving to Done.

question: What's the process for submitting time off, and how far in advance do I need to request it?
reference_answer: You should submit PTO (Paid Time Off) requests through TimeTrax, which integrates with Workday, at least 14 days in advance. TimeTrax will also automatically flag any overtime hours during peak seasons like March for approval.

question: How do I submit a request for a one-time analysis and when can I expect to get results?
reference_answer: Submit a ticket in Jira under the ANALYTICS project with the label 'data-request', including your business question, required metrics, deadline, and intended use. The Analytics team will triage your request during Monday morning standup, and simple requests that take less than 4 hours will be committed the same day with a 2 business day SLA, while complex analyses typically take 5-10 business days.

question: I need to report a bug in ClaimsFlow and want to make sure it gets to the right team. Which Slack channel should I use?
reference_answer: You should post in #claimsflow-dev, which is used for ClaimsFlow development, bug reports, and deployment updates where Platform Engineering and Claims Ops collaborate. You can post error logs and testing results there for the team to review.

question: What should I do if I receive a critical incident alert and haven't made any progress after 10 minutes?
reference_answer: You should escalate to the secondary on-call engineer after 10 minutes without progress on P1 incidents. You can find the secondary on-call engineer listed in the PagerDuty rotation.
